pointers.sentence: `Command.handle` turns its labels into an ordered dictionary of application configurations, each mapped to a list of models, or to `None` for all of them; with no labels it takes every application that has a models module (`django/core/management/commands/dumpdata.py:Command.handle`).

A model is dumped where `ConnectionRouter.allow_migrate_model` allows it on the database, which asks only the routers, so an unmanaged model is dumped like any other (`django/db/utils.py:ConnectionRouter.allow_migrate_model`).

The rows are the default manager's, or the base manager's with `--all`, ordered by primary key and read with `QuerySet.iterator`, given a chunk size of 2000 where the manager prefetches, which `iterator` then requires (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.iterator`).

Written as a primary key, a foreign key is not looked up when it is loaded: the value is converted, and the row goes in whether or not its target is there yet (`django/core/serializers/base.py:deserialize_fk_value`).
Only with that option does dumpdata sort its models, with `sort_dependencies` (`django/core/serializers/__init__.py:sort_dependencies`).

`Command.parse_name` takes the last dotted part as a compression if it is one, and then requires the last part that remains, where a dot precedes it, to be a public format, refusing the label otherwise; so a name with a dot in it is given with its format (`django/core/management/commands/loaddata.py:Command.parse_name`).

`Command.fixture_dirs` lists the `"fixtures"` directory of each installed application that has one, in the order of `INSTALLED_APPS` (only that of `--app` where it is given), then `FIXTURE_DIRS`, then the current directory; `FIXTURE_DIRS` naming a directory twice, or an application's own, is `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/core/management/commands/loaddata.py:Command.fixture_dirs`).

In each directory `Command.find_fixtures` keeps the files whose names `Command.get_targets` allows: the name, optionally the alias of the database being loaded, a format, and optionally a compression (`django/core/management/commands/loaddata.py:Command.find_fixtures`).
`Command.handle` runs the load inside `atomic`, so a fixture that fails undoes every object loaded before it (`django/core/management/commands/loaddata.py:Command.handle`).

`Command.loaddata` finds the first label's files before turning foreign key checks off, which its comment says is expensive on some databases, and then loads each label inside `BaseDatabaseWrapper.constraint_checks_disabled` (`django/core/management/commands/loaddata.py:Command.loaddata`).

An object whose natural foreign key names a row not yet loaded has that field deferred, `DEFER_FIELD`, and is saved without it; after the last label, `DeserializedObject.save_deferred_fields` looks the key up again, now refusing a missing row, and saves the object again (`django/core/serializers/base.py:DeserializedObject.save_deferred_fields`).
The documentation requires such a foreign key to have `null=True` (`docs/topics/serialization.txt`).

Then `BaseDatabaseWrapper.check_constraints` checks the tables of the models whose objects were saved, and where anything was loaded the statements of the backend's `BaseDatabaseOperations.sequence_reset_sql` move each model's sequence to the largest key in its table, on PostgreSQL and Oracle; the base class, which SQLite and MySQL keep, writes none (`django/core/management/commands/loaddata.py:Command.reset_sequences`) ([The connection object: `BaseDatabaseWrapper` and what a backend provides](../backends/wrapper.md#foreign-key-checks-switched-off-constraint_checks_disabled), [Introspection: reading the schema back](../schema/introspection.md#sequences-sequence_reset_by_name_sql-and-sequence_reset_sql)).

`DeserializedObject.save` calls `Model.save_base` with `raw=True`: the model's own `save` is not called, and the receivers of `pre_save`, `post_save` and `m2m_changed` are told the save is raw ([Serialization: `serialize`, `deserialize` and `DeserializedObject`](serializers.md)) (`django/core/serializers/base.py:DeserializedObject.save`).
The documentation suggests that a receiver reaching related fields the load has not supplied return at once when raw is true (`docs/topics/db/fixtures.txt`).
Many-to-many rows set from a fixture send `m2m_changed` with `raw=True` (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
